summary: This work develops numerical simulation methods for microwave photon detection using superconducting Kerr parametric resonators operated near the parametric instability threshold. The authors solve Heisenberg-Langevin and Fokker-Planck equations in a semiclassical approximation to characterize switching dynamics and show that detection efficiency is enhanced by probe signals down to single-photon levels.
motivation: Parametric devices at criticality exhibit heightened sensitivity to weak perturbations, offering a promising avenue for single-photon detection in superconducting quantum systems. Understanding the switching mechanisms and detection performance near the phase transition boundary is essential for practical implementations in quantum information processing.
method: Semiclassical treatment of a parametrically pumped Kerr oscillator via Heisenberg-Langevin equations, using separation of slow and fast quadratures to derive an effective potential analogous to Landau free energy in phase transitions. Fokker-Planck equation solved numerically and analytically to compute switching probabilities and detection efficiency for coherent probe states.
result: At operational point with $|\alpha|/(\kappa+\gamma)=0.506$, $\Delta/(2\pi)=0.748$ MHz, $K/(\kappa+\gamma)=-3.12\times10^{-5}$: dark count probability $p_{\text{dark}}\approx0.14$, single-photon switching probability $P_{1^+}\approx0.52$, and detection efficiency $\eta\approx0.58$ for $n̄=1$ photon pulses; analytical solutions for Kerr-free resonators ($K=0$) confirm the approximations.
